On Wed, Oct 24, 2012 at 12:42 PM, Nicolás Gálvez <conc...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello, 

I am in the process of undertaking a second season of survey out of a total of 4, where I will be gathering detection/non-detection data on a territorial small cat with camera traps.

During a first season  I surveyed 100 sites.

However, I want to expand to another an adjacent area to improve comparison in terms of the research question.   It is not a completely different area, it is more of a gradient where I will obtain more variability in the landscape variables that I am looking into.

The issue is that logistically, I can only effectively survey 160 sites.  So I was thinking on randomly choosing 80 from the first 100 sites (First season), and pick 80 from the new area.  Then the remaining seasons sample the same sites (160). 

Any thoughts on possible problems?  One of my worries is the random selection of the 80 sites out of the 100  and how this could possible bias the comparison with the 1st season.

Would really appreciate if someone has ideas on unexpected problems with data analysis or further suggestions.

Thanks!

Nico
